title: Micro examples: compact SDK patterns for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, and CLI
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a set of compact, easy-to-reuse code examples and minimal templates that show advanced Redwood SDK patterns across Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (Next.js), Go (HTTP server), and a cross-language CLI. Focus on streaming ergonomics, retry/backoff strategies, cancellation/resumption, and lightweight production guidance.
rationale: Existing example collections are comprehensive but large. Teams benefit from small, copy-pasteable micro-examples that highlight one pattern at a time (e.g., server-sent streaming handling, exponential backoff with jitter, token-level cost tracing). These will improve onboarding and reduce support questions.
scope: Deliver one minimal app per runtime (Next.js server route / app-router action, FastAPI endpoint, Go HTTP handler, and a language-agnostic CLI wrapper). Each example must demonstrate: streaming generation with partial outputs, robust retry + idempotency keys, graceful cancellation via context/signals, basic prefix caching hook, and minimal tests and README.
deliverables: nextjs-edge-streaming-example.tsx - minimal server action + client consumption
fastapi-streaming-endpoint.py - background task + streaming chunk wrapper
go-http-streamer.go - context-cancelled streaming handler with KV cache demo
cli-generate.sh/cli-go/cli-py - examples for invocations with progress bars
common README.md - copyable snippets and pattern explanations
unit smoke tests and CI snippet (GitHub Actions example)
Quickstart shell script to scaffold project
acceptance_criteria: All four examples run locally with environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY and documented setup
Streaming examples emit incremental tokens usable by client-side code and show progress indicators
Retry examples include idempotency key pattern and configurable backoff policy with sample settings
Cancellation flows terminate token streaming and free server resources within SLA (under 2s after cancel signal)
Minimal tests exist and CI workflow runs and passes
Examples are under 200 lines per file where possible and include inline comments explaining key SDK calls

notes: Prefer Next.js app router server actions for edge-friendly streaming; include variant for Node server if needed
Show both SDK streaming iterator and low-level HTTP chunk reader to help teams migrating older code
Use exponential backoff with full jitter (cap at 5s) and sample wrapper function in each language
For KV cache demo, use a simple in-memory LRU in examples but comment where to replace with production cache
Keep secret handling minimal; recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY via .env and avoid baking keys into examples
